subject: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan

Team —

Quick context: Helix Finance wants to move from pilot to production, and the legal/procurement team has made a prioritized list of requirements that they have tied to signing. The three asks at the top are: 
- tenant-level routing isolation (logical tenancy + dedicated routing lanes)
- audit export (s3 export + 90-day retention, format CSV/JSON)
- predictable warm-pool guarantee for peak hours (they want a burst SLA)

Attached: SOW draft and our usage forecast from the pilot. They indicate $450k ARR on contract and procurement is pressing for a delivery timeline before mid-September to align with their procurement cycle.

We need a clear internal answer for what we can commit to and by when. Ask: can Product/Eng either commit to a full implementation timeline (tenant isolation + audit export + warm-pool) or propose a reduced minimal deliverable that gets them to sign (e.g., audit export + residency fallback + documented migration plan)?

Please reply with:
- a high-level scope that Product can accept as the "signing scope"
- engineering-level estimate (rough weeks + risk)
- a recommended earliest sprint/start date

I'm marking this high urgency because Ben needs to update Helix procurement by Thursday EOD PT.

Attachments: SOW-Helix-v3.pdf, helix-usage-forecast.xlsx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan

Thanks Jordan —

FWIW my priority here is to get Helix comfortable enough to sign while minimizing product risk and avoiding long-term maintenance holes. Quick clarifying questions before we commit:
- What exactly do they mean by "tenant-level routing isolation" — are they asking for physical isolation (dedicated GPU pools) or logical routing + affinity (pinning requests to pools)?
- For audit export: is S3 the only acceptable target, and do they require an automated daily export or on-demand support?
- Warm-pool guarantee: is this a billing/financial SLA ask or a hard latency/availability SLA during defined windows?

From a product standpoint I'd prefer a two-phased signing scope:
Phase 1 (signing scope, minimal): audit export + logical tenant pinning (no infra-level dedicated pools) + documented fallback plan for capacity constraints.
Phase 2 (post-sign): hard SLA options and warm-pool guarantees (implemented as a paid add-on / dedicated capacity).

If Eng can confirm that Phase 1 is achievable in ~3 weeks of focused work we can use that to close the deal and then queue Phase 2 for a prioritized roadmap item. Marcus — can you weigh in on feasibility and rough effort?

Also suggest a 30-minute alignment call with Alex from Helix this week so we can get their exact acceptance criteria documented. Ben – can you set that up?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Group PM, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan

Marissa / Jordan —

Tech assessment (short):
- Full "tenant isolation" with physical/dedicated GPU pools requires infra and scheduler work and touches provisioning, autoscaler, and billing hooks. Rough estimate: 6 weeks dev + 2 weeks QA + coordination with infra ops. Risk: capacity fragmentation and higher unit costs; requires reserved capacity contract to be meaningful.

- Logical tenant pinning + audit export + residency fallback (what Marissa calls Phase 1) is much more tractable. We can implement:
  * request affinity/pinning layer (routing metadata + KV cache hints)
  * export pipeline (scheduled JSON/CSV export to S3 with schema and incremental deltas)
  * a documented fallback flow when capacity is constrained (route to compatible model variant + notification)

Estimate for Phase 1: 3-4 weeks (2.5 dev weeks + 1 week integration/QA). Blockers: S3 permissions + cross-account key exchange if Helix requires a customer-owned bucket; we'll need security to sign off.

Attached: implementation-outline.md, effort-estimate.xlsx (high-level milestones). Tentative timeline if we start planning week of Sep 6:
- Sep 6–Sep 24: dev milestones (pinning + export)
- Sep 27–Oct 1: QA and customer validation

Caveats: this will not provide a hard warm-pool SLA. If Helix insists on absolute burst guarantees we need a separate Dedicated capacity workstream (adds 4–6 weeks).

If Product is comfortable with Phase 1 as the signing scope, we can lock a planning slot and break down tickets this week.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@helix.com>, Procurement Team <procure@helix.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan

Quick update from Helix side — Alex confirmed today that procurement is on a tight cycle and their internal board wants a signed contract by Sep 15. They told me they would accept the following as a signing condition:
- Phase 1 scope (audit export + logical tenant pinning + documented fallback)
- A stated timeline in the SOW with firm milestone dates (even if Phase 2 is optional)

Alex, tagging you to confirm that the above matches what you communicated. I can drop the updated SOW and DocuSign link if Product/Eng sign off on Phase 1 timeline.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/ABCDEF123456

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix activation: request for sprint slot and gated delivery plan

Thanks all — alignment below and next steps: 

Decision: we will go with Phase 1 as the signing scope (audit export + logical tenant pinning + documented fallback). Marcus's timeline looks reasonable.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft acceptance criteria and SOW language for Phase 1 (due Fri Aug 27)
- Marcus: finalize dev plan and ticket breakdown; confirm any security permissions needed (by Aug 30)
- Ben: update Helix procurement with Phase 1 timeline and send updated SOW / DocuSign link once Marissa provides wording
- Grace: prepare CSM onboarding notes and runbook for fallback behavior to include in handoff docs

I'll set a 30-minute internal check on Monday Sep 6 to confirm sprint cadence and signal to Eng to start. If anyone sees blockers to the above commitments, flag immediately.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
